subject: Polity
description: Lok Sabha procedures — Question Hour, Zero Hour, motions (no-confidence, censure, adjournment), Speaker's role, voting and divisions.

questions.stem: QUESTION HOUR in Lok Sabha is held during the:

options.option_text: First hour of every sitting (11 AM-12 noon)
Last hour of any sitting (5-6 PM)
Lunch hour daily for one hour (option here)
Once a week on Mondays only (option here)

questions.explanation: QUESTION HOUR — first hour of LOK SABHA sittings (11:00 AM to 12:00 noon usually). Members ask QUESTIONS to MINISTERS regarding their portfolios; ministers (or junior ministers) provide answers. THREE TYPES OF QUESTIONS: (1) STARRED — receive ORAL answer; supplementary questions allowed; marked with asterisk (*). (2) UNSTARRED — receive WRITTEN answer; no supplementary questions. (3) SHORT-NOTICE — for matter of urgent public importance; must give 10 days' notice; rules at Speaker's discretion. PROCEDURE: notice must be given 21 DAYS in advance; Speaker decides admissibility. PURPOSE: a fundamental tool of executive ACCOUNTABILITY — ministers face direct questioning by elected MPs. RECENT TRENDS: in last few years, Question Hour has been DISRUPTED frequently due to opposition protests; ~50% loss of question hour during turbulent sessions. ZERO HOUR follows immediately AFTER Question Hour (noon to 1 PM); not constitutionally provided but a parliamentary CONVENTION since 1962. NOT FOUND IN CONSTITUTION: Question Hour is governed by the RULES OF PROCEDURE of LOK SABHA, NOT the Constitution itself. SPEAKER's role: presides over Question Hour, decides admissibility, expunges objectionable language. PYQ FREQUENCY: Question Hour basics in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC polity 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: ZERO HOUR in Indian Parliament is:

options.option_text: Time after Question Hour for urgent matters
Time when no work is conducted
First hour of monsoon session there

questions.explanation: ZERO HOUR — informal parliamentary convention; immediately follows QUESTION HOUR — runs typically from 12 NOON to 1 PM (in Lok Sabha) — used by MPs to RAISE MATTERS OF URGENT PUBLIC IMPORTANCE. ORIGIN: started in 1962 (an Indian innovation; not in any other Parliament's procedure). NOT MENTIONED in Rules of Procedure or Constitution; purely a CONVENTION. NAME 'ZERO HOUR': because it begins at the 'zeroth hour' (12:00 noon, between session segments). PROCEDURE: MPs give NOTICE to Speaker (between 10 AM and 12 PM same day) about issues they want to raise; Speaker selects which to permit; each issue limited to ~3 minutes typically. TYPICAL ISSUES: local emergencies, accidents, prices, controversies, drought, floods, regional concerns. CRITICISM: often becomes a platform for grandstanding; serious legislation suffers when much of session is consumed by Zero Hour drama. CONTRAST WITH OTHER MOTIONS: (1) ADJOURNMENT MOTION — formal, demands suspension of business; needs 50 MP support; usually rejected by Speaker. (2) HALF-AN-HOUR DISCUSSION — pre-arranged; held after the day's business concludes. (3) PRIVILEGE MOTION — about breach of privilege. (4) CALLING-ATTENTION MOTION — shorter version of half-hour, called by Speaker. PYQ FREQUENCY: Zero Hour in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION can be moved against:

options.option_text: Council of Ministers (CoM, govt as whole)
Speaker of the Lok Sabha alone (option here)
Individual MP for any reason (option here)

questions.explanation: NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION — moved against the COUNCIL OF MINISTERS (i.e., the government as a whole, headed by the PRIME MINISTER) under Article 75(3) read with Rules. RULES: (1) Notice in writing by MP. (2) ADMISSIBLE only if 50 MEMBERS support (in 543-member House). (3) Speaker decides admissibility. (4) DEBATE typically 2-3 days; PM must speak. (5) DIVISION (vote) at end. PASSAGE: if motion gets MAJORITY of MEMBERS PRESENT AND VOTING → government LOSES confidence → must RESIGN (PM submits resignation to President). KEY: a successful no-confidence motion automatically dismisses the entire government, NOT just one minister. NUMBER of NO-CONFIDENCE MOTIONS in INDIA: ~28 since 1947 (in Lok Sabha); only a HANDFUL successful — most famous is the FALL OF VAJPAYEE'S 13-DAY GOVERNMENT (1996, lost by 1 vote — 269 to 270). RECENT: Modi government faced no-confidence motions July 2018 and August 2023 — both DEFEATED easily (BJP majority). DIFFERENT MOTIONS: (1) NO-CONFIDENCE — against entire CoM. (2) CENSURE MOTION — against entire CoM or individual minister; doesn't bring down govt; expresses disapproval; requires reason. (3) ADJOURNMENT MOTION — to discuss urgent matter; doesn't bring down govt. (4) MOTION OF THANKS — on President's address; convention. PYQ FREQUENCY: no-confidence motion in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Who decides whether a Bill is a MONEY BILL or not?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 110 — SPEAKER OF THE LOK SABHA decides whether a bill is a MONEY BILL. The Speaker's CERTIFICATION is FINAL — Article 110(3) explicitly states this; the decision cannot be questioned in courts (a contentious area). MONEY BILL CHARACTERISTICS: deals exclusively with: (a) Imposition, abolition, alteration of TAXES. (b) Borrowing/lending of money by GoI. (c) Custody of Consolidated Fund / Contingency Fund. (d) Appropriation of money from Consolidated Fund. (e) Any matter incidental to above. NOT covered (mere fee for service, fine, etc.) → not a money bill. KEY PROCEDURE for MONEY BILL: (1) Introduced ONLY in LOK SABHA (not Rajya Sabha) — Article 109. (2) Cannot be amended by Rajya Sabha; only RECOMMENDATIONS allowed. (3) Lok Sabha may accept or reject Rajya Sabha's recommendations; if rejected, bill becomes law as Lok Sabha passed it. (4) Rajya Sabha must return within 14 days; else deemed passed. (5) President can ONLY ASSENT or WITHHOLD assent (cannot return for reconsideration). CONTROVERSY: ADHAAR ACT 2016 was certified as Money Bill — challenged in SC (Puttaswamy case 2018, K.S. Puttaswamy v. UoI on Adhaar). SC upheld certification (4-1) but warned against overuse of Money Bill route. RECENT (2023): Speaker has certified some controversial bills as Money Bills, drawing criticism. PYQ FREQUENCY: money bill rules in UPSC, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which official in Lok Sabha presides when both Speaker AND Deputy Speaker are absent?
questions.explanation: PANEL OF CHAIRPERSONS — Article 95(1): when both SPEAKER and DEPUTY SPEAKER are absent, a member from the PANEL OF CHAIRPERSONS (nominated by Speaker, normally a list of ~10 senior MPs) presides over the Lok Sabha. ARTICLE 95: 'In the absence of both Speaker and Deputy Speaker, such person as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the House, or, if no such person is present, such other person as may be determined by the House.' PRO TEM SPEAKER (Article 99): different role — appointed at the START of a NEW Lok Sabha (after general elections) by the President; presides only over the first sitting until a new SPEAKER is elected from members. SPEAKER's election: in the first sitting of newly-elected Lok Sabha; pro tem Speaker (usually senior-most MP) presides. SPEAKER'S TENURE: continues until dissolution of Lok Sabha or his/her resignation/removal. RAJYA SABHA equivalent — VICE PRESIDENT is ex-officio CHAIRMAN (Art 89); DEPUTY CHAIRMAN is elected by RS members. When both VP and Deputy Chairman absent, panel of vice-chairmen presides. CURRENT (2026): LS Speaker = Om Birla (2nd term, 2024-29); Deputy Speaker = vacant since 2019 (controversial). PYQ FREQUENCY: presiding officers procedure in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: What is the QUORUM required for Lok Sabha sittings?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 100(3) — QUORUM (minimum members required) for Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha = 1/10th of TOTAL membership of the House. For LOK SABHA (543 members) → quorum = 55 (1/10 = 54.3, rounded up). For RAJYA SABHA (245 members) → quorum = 25 (245/10 = 24.5, rounded up). IF QUORUM IS NOT MET: presiding officer SUSPENDS the sitting until quorum is restored. CRITICISM: low quorum requirement means most decisions are taken by less than 10% of MPs in attendance — concerns about democratic legitimacy. PRACTICAL OBSERVATION: actual attendance often LOW; some bills passed with attendance ~50-60 MPs. SPEAKER'S RESPONSE: usually doesn't suspend sitting unless someone formally raises 'point of quorum'. CONSTITUTIONAL VS LEGISLATIVE quorum: (1) FOR PASSING ORDINARY LEGISLATION: quorum (1/10) + simple majority of those present. (2) FOR CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS (Art 368): special majority — 2/3 of present + 50% of total membership. (3) FOR REMOVAL OF JUDGES, etc.: also special majority. PYQ FREQUENCY: quorum + voting requirements in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC polity — 1-2× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise constitutional numbers + procedural details.

questions.stem: An ADJOURNMENT MOTION in Lok Sabha is moved to:

options.option_text: Discuss matter of urgent public importance

questions.explanation: ADJOURNMENT MOTION — extraordinary procedure that, if PASSED, suspends the day's business to discuss a SPECIFIC MATTER OF URGENT PUBLIC IMPORTANCE. Used to bring govt's attention to a serious issue (riots, accidents, financial scams, security failures). PROCEDURE: (1) Notice in writing to Speaker before 10 AM. (2) Topic must be DEFINITE, RECENT, of URGENT public importance, requiring URGENT discussion (not subject of pending judicial proceedings). (3) Speaker decides admissibility. (4) Requires SUPPORT of 50 MPs. (5) Discussion can last for max 2.5 hours. (6) MOTION USUALLY DEFEATED — symbolic value rather than legal effect. ELEMENT OF CENSURE: passing of the motion implies CRITICISM of govt — strong political weapon. SAMPLE INSTANCES: 1947-2024 — many adjournment motions on partition violence (1947), Indo-China war (1962), Chinese aggression (2020), Pulwama (2019), railway accidents, Delhi riots, etc. CRITICISM: in BJP-majority Lok Sabha, recent admissibility of opposition's adjournment motions has been low; opposition resorts to Zero Hour or media. CONTRAST: NO-CONFIDENCE motion brings DOWN govt; ADJOURNMENT motion is a censure-like tool that doesn't directly affect govt's continuation. ADJOURNMENT-SINE-DIE: ending of a session indefinitely — different concept; done by Speaker. PYQ FREQUENCY: adjournment motion in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.
